title: Developmental bioelectricity preceded and gave rise to nervous systems

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Developmental bioelectricity preceded and gave rise to nervous systems

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Developmental bioelectrics is an ancient precursor of nervous systems: evolution first used analog bioelectric dynamics to position body configuration in developmental morphospace, long before some cells specialized in fast digital spiking to control behaviour in 3D space.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Evolution first exploited this to enable cell groups to position the body configuration in developmental morphospace, long before some cells specialized to use very fast, digital spiking as neural networks for control of behavior as movement in 3-dimensional space (Fields et al., 2020).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Evolutionary Aspects › Somatic Bioelectrics Reveals the Origin of Complex Cognitive Systems”. Scope: Evolution of bioelectric signalling and nervous systems in animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-25: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative genomics can test temporal ordering of molecular components and specialized nervous systems. It has limited power to establish that developmental pattern control was the ancestral function that gave rise to nervous systems.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the phylogenetic distribution, ancestral functions, and developmental versus neural deployment of bioelectric machinery, testing whether multicellular pattern-control roles predate specialized nervous systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The behavioral-versus-morphospace framing is interpretive.

Gene ancestry does not identify ancestral physiological function.

Extant taxa imperfectly reconstruct the sequence of functional innovations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.5
data existence: 0.78

discriminating power: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public genomes can show that many bioelectric gene families occur in animals without neurons and in close unicellular relatives, which bears on which hardware came first. The claim also says evolution used analog bioelectric dynamics to position body configuration before neural spiking. That use is not a column in the genome matrices, so gene age is only a partial test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map ion-channel, connexin, and innexin families onto aneural animals and their unicellular relatives versus the origin of neurons; precedence of the genes holds if the families are present before nervous systems, which still leaves their developmental use untested.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Gene presence in a sponge or placozoan does not show that the genes were used to place the body in morphospace.

Channels have many functions besides positional control, so their age is compatible with other histories.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.65
